title: Deepfake Scams and Fakes
about: Spot the red flags of a faked voice or video, and check who is really there.

cards.prompt: Your phone rings from a number you don't know. Some scammers now use AI to copy people's voices.

steps.text: It sounds exactly like your grandma: "I've lost my purse and I'm stuck. Please send me money now, and don't worry your parents." What do you do?

choices.text: Send the money: it's her voice
choices.consequence: Voices can be copied with AI. Money sent to a scammer is usually gone for good.

choices.text: Say you'll call her back, and hang up
choices.consequence: Good: hanging up stops the pressure. Now check.

choices.text: Keep chatting to find out more
choices.consequence: Scammers are good at talking. The longer you stay on, the more they can pressure you. It's safer to hang up.

steps.text: You've hung up. How do you check it was really her?

choices.text: Call Grandma on the number you already have
choices.consequence: She answers at home, perfectly fine. It was a scam, and you stopped it.

choices.text: Call back the number that just rang
choices.consequence: That number belongs to the caller, so they'd just answer again. Use the number you already know.

choices.text: Tell a trusted adult what happened
choices.consequence: Good choice: an adult can call Grandma on her real number with you, and help report the scam.

cards.hint: A familiar voice can be copied. Is there a way to reach the real Grandma that the caller can't fake?
cards.explanation: A new number, **hurry**, **money** and **keep it from your parents** are all red flags. Hang up, then check using the number **you already have**, or with a **trusted adult**. Never call back the number that rang you.

cards.title: Fake voices and faces
cards.body:
AI can copy a voice from real recordings, sometimes just a few seconds of video posted online. That's a **voice clone**. A faked video or picture is a **deepfake**. You can't always tell by looking or listening.

The red flags still work: **hurry**, **keep it secret**, **money, gift cards or codes**, and **a new number**.

**What to do:** hang up or stop replying. Contact them on the number **you already have**, or ask a trusted adult.

items.label: Don't tell Mum, just send it
Buy gift cards and send the codes
It's me, I've got a new number
Send it in the next 5 minutes!
See you at practice on Saturday
Can you bring my jumper home?
Meeting moved to 3 pm, same room

cards.hint: Look for the four tricks: hurry, secrets, money or codes, and a new number.
cards.nudge: Check each message for pressure to hurry, to keep a secret, to send money or codes, or a new number.
cards.explanation: Rushing you, asking for **secrets**, **gift cards or codes**, and a **new number** are all red flags, whoever the message seems to be from. Plans and favours are normal.

cards.prompt: A video call from your friend's account asks you to send a code that just arrived by text. Their face and voice look right. What's the **best** thing to do?

options.text: Don't send it. Check with your friend another way, like their usual number
Send it: their face and voice both match, so it must really be them
options.nudge: Faces and voices can be faked with AI. The request for a code is the red flag. How else could you reach your friend?

options.text: Ask them to explain why it is so urgent, and then send it
options.nudge: A scammer can always make up a good reason, and hurry is a red flag. Is there a way to check it's really them first?

cards.hint: A face and voice can be faked. What can't a scammer fake?
cards.explanation: A deepfake can copy a face and voice, but it can't answer on your friend's **usual number**. Asking for a code is a red flag, so don't send it: check another way first. Sign-in codes are never safe to share.

cards.prompt:
If someone makes or shares a fake picture or video of you, even a fake nude or sexual image, it's **not your fault**, and you won't be in trouble for asking for help.

**Don't share it** any further, even to show someone. **Don't pay** or send anything they ask for. **Save evidence**: screenshot the messages, the account name and the web address, but never the image itself. **Tell a trusted adult**.

Sort what to **do**, and what **not** to do.

items.label: Share it to show your friends
Save a copy of the image itself

cards.hint: What helps you, and what helps whoever made the fake? The prompt lists what to do.
cards.nudge: Saving evidence means the messages and the account, not the picture. And you never have to deal with this alone.
cards.explanation: **Do:** tell a trusted adult, and screenshot the messages and account. **Don't:** share it, save the image itself, pay, or keep it to yourself. None of this is your fault.

cards.prompt:
**Report** a fake image of you to the app, and to the government's **eSafety Commissioner** (esafety.gov.au/report), which can help get fake nude or sexual images taken down.

If you're **under 18** and someone is threatening to share it, or asking you for sexual images or money, report it to the **ACCCE** (Australian Centre to Counter Child Exploitation) too: accce.gov.au/report.

steps.text: Jo is 15. Someone made a fake picture of Jo and says they'll share it unless Jo pays. Jo has told a trusted adult. Where should they report it?

choices.text: The app, eSafety and the ACCCE
choices.consequence: Right. eSafety can help get the image taken down, and the ACCCE helps under-18s who are being threatened. Jo won't be in trouble.

choices.text: Just the app: it's a fake, so it's not that serious
choices.consequence: Fakes are serious too. eSafety can help get fake nude or sexual images taken down, and because Jo is under 18 and being threatened, the ACCCE should hear about it as well.

choices.text: Nowhere: Jo might get in trouble for reporting it
choices.consequence: Jo won't be in trouble for asking for help. It's not Jo's fault. Reporting to the app, eSafety and the ACCCE is how it gets stopped.

cards.hint: Look back at the prompt: who to report to, and what changes when you're under 18 and someone is threatening you.
cards.explanation: Report to the **app** and to the **eSafety Commissioner** (esafety.gov.au/report), which can help get fake nude or sexual images taken down. Jo is under 18 and being threatened, so the **ACCCE** (accce.gov.au/report) too. It's never Jo's fault.

cards.prompt:
Some families agree a **family safe word**: a secret word just for emergencies, never posted online.

A caller sounds just like your brother. He can't say the family safe word, and he keeps rushing you. What now?

options.text: Hang up, and call him on the number you already have
Keep going: he's probably just forgotten it in a panic
options.nudge: Forgetting is possible, but a voice can be copied. A wrong safe word plus hurry is exactly when to check another way.

options.text: Give him a clue about the word so he can remember it
options.nudge: A clue could hand the word to a scammer. How could you reach the real person instead?

cards.hint: A safe word is a check that a copied voice can't pass. If the check fails, what's the safest way to reach the real person?
cards.explanation: No safe word and lots of hurry: hang up, and call him on the number **you already have**. If it was really him, he'll answer. Never give away the safe word, even as a clue.

cards.prompt: A video message arrives from an account with your coach's name and face.

steps.text: "Send me a photo of you in your uniform for the team page. Keep it between us." It really looks like your coach. It could be a deepfake. What do you do?

choices.consequence: "Keep it between us" is a red flag, even from someone you know. A real coach wouldn't ask you to keep secrets.

choices.text: Don't reply, and tell a trusted adult
choices.consequence: Exactly. An adult can check with the real coach. Secrets and requests for photos are red flags, whatever face is on the screen.

choices.text: Ask them to send another video to prove it
choices.consequence: A deepfake can make another video. Check another way: through a trusted adult, or the coach's usual contact.

cards.hint: Look past the face. Which red flag is in the message itself?
cards.explanation: The face might be real or fake, but **"keep it between us"** is a red flag either way. Don't reply, and **tell a trusted adult**, who can check with the real coach. Another video proves nothing.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- AI can fake voices and faces. The red flags still work.
- Hang up, then check on the number you already have.
- A fake of you: not your fault. Tell, save evidence, report.

Want to talk? In Australia: **Kids Helpline** 1800 55 1800 (up to 25) or **Lifeline** 13 11 14, any time.
